questionText:
The baseline execution time of a program on a $2\text{ GHz}$ single core machine is $100$ nanoseconds ($ns$). The code corresponding to $90\%$ of the execution time can be fully parallelized. The overhead for using an additional core is $10\text{ ns}$ when running on a multicore system. Assume that all cores in the multicore system run their share of the parallelized code for an equal amount of time.

The number of cores that minimize the execution time of the program is _________
explanation:
Step 1: Understand the baseline components of execution time.
Total baseline execution time $T_1 = 100\text{ ns}$.
Parallelizable portion ($90\%$ of $100\text{ ns}$) = $90\text{ ns}$.
Non-parallelizable (serial) portion ($10\%$ of $100\text{ ns}$) = $10\text{ ns}$.

Step 2: Express execution time as a function of the number of cores $p$.
For $p$ cores, the time taken by the parallel part is $\frac{90}{p}\text{ ns}$.
The overhead for using an additional core is $10\text{ ns}$ per additional core, which equals $10 \times (p - 1)\text{ ns}$.
Thus, total execution time $T(p)$ for $p$ cores is given by:
$T(p) = \text{Serial time} + \text{Parallel time} + \text{Overhead time}$
$T(p) = 10 + \frac{90}{p} + 10(p - 1) = \frac{90}{p} + 10p$

Step 3: Calculate $T(p)$ for integer values of $p$.
For $p = 1$: $T(1) = \frac{90}{1} + 10(1) = 90 + 10 = 100\text{ ns}$
For $p = 2$: $T(2) = \frac{90}{2} + 10(2) = 45 + 20 = 65\text{ ns}$
For $p = 3$: $T(3) = \frac{90}{3} + 10(3) = 30 + 30 = 60\text{ ns}$
For $p = 4$: $T(4) = \frac{90}{4} + 10(4) = 22.5 + 40 = 62.5\text{ ns}$

Since $T(3) = 60\text{ ns}$ is the minimum execution time, the optimal number of cores is 3.
